userStories.title: Validate shell interception without trusting provider stdout
acceptanceCriteria: validateShellRewrite returns { kind: 'rewritten', command: 'rtk bun test a.test.ts', provider: 'rtk' } for original 'bun test a.test.ts' and that candidate.
validateShellRewrite returns a rewritten result for original 'FOO=1 bun test' and candidate 'FOO=1 rtk bun test', where the insertion follows the assignment token.
validateShellRewrite returns a rewritten result for original 'bun test; git status' and candidate 'rtk bun test; rtk git status', an insertion in each of two segments.
validateShellRewrite returns a rewritten result for original 'cd pkg && bun test' and candidate 'cd pkg && rtk bun test', where only the second segment is rewritten.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'cat src/a.ts' and candidate 'rtk read src/a.ts'.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'cd pkg&&bun test' and candidate 'cd pkg && rtk bun test', because spacing changed.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'uv run pytest -q' and candidate 'uv run rtk pytest -q', because the insertion is not at the command word.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'git log --oneline | head -5' and candidate 'rtk git log --oneline | head -5', because the rewritten segment feeds a pipe.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original "bun test 'a b.ts'" and candidate 'rtk bun test "a b.ts"', because quoting changed.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'rtk bun test' and candidate 'rtk rtk bun test'.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'bun test' and candidate 'rtk bun test; rm -rf .', when the candidate appends a segment.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'cat x | grep y' and candidate 'cat x | rtk grep y', because the rewritten segment reads a pipe.
validateShellRewrite returns kind 'declined' for original 'bun test $(id)' and candidate 'rtk bun test $(id)', when the original does not lex.
validateShellRewrite returns { kind: 'unchanged' } when the candidate equals the original.
validateShellRewrite returns an unchanged or declined result it is given without modification.
interceptShell('bun test', root, undefined) returns { command: 'bun test', rewritten: false }.
interceptShell returns the original command with rewritten: false when the interceptor has no interceptShell method.
interceptShell calls the interceptor's interceptShell once with { kind: 'shell', command, cwd, site: 'bash' }.
interceptShell returns { command: 'rtk bun test', provider: 'rtk', rewritten: true } when the interceptor answers rewritten with a candidate that passes validation.
interceptShell returns the original command with rewritten: false when the interceptor answers a candidate that fails validation.
interceptShell returns the original command with rewritten: false when the interceptor's interceptShell throws.
When importing from @/execution/command-interceptor, then interceptShell and validateShellRewrite resolve to the shell seam's exported functions.

routing.reasoning: Novel shell-command validation at an access-control trust boundary; errors could execute provider-authored shell code.

userStories.title: Configure and provide rtk shell rewrites
acceptanceCriteria: ExecutionConfigSchema parsed with no commandInterceptor yields commandInterceptor.bash.enabled === false.
DEFAULT_CONFIG.execution.commandInterceptor.bash.enabled is false.
ExecutionConfigSchema parses commandInterceptor: { enabled: true, bash: { enabled: true } } with bash.enabled === true.

ExecutionConfigSchema rejects commandInterceptor: { enabled: false, bash: { enabled: true } } with issue message 'execution.commandInterceptor.bash.enabled requires execution.commandInterceptor.enabled'.
ExecutionConfigSchema rejects an unknown key inside commandInterceptor.bash.
When reading FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS['execution.commandInterceptor.bash.enabled'], then its value is a non-empty string.

createRtkInterceptor({ enabled: true, verbs: [], bash: true, _deps }) interceptShell returns { kind: 'rewritten', command: 'rtk bun test', provider: 'rtk' } for bun test when rewrite returns { exitCode: 3, stdout: 'rtk bun test\n', timedOut: false }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns a rewritten result when rewrite returns { exitCode: 0, stdout: 'rtk bun test', timedOut: false }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } when rewrite returns { exitCode: 1, stdout: '', timedOut: false }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } when rewrite returns { exitCode: 3, stdout: the original command, timedOut: false }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } when rewrite returns { exitCode: 3, stdout: '', timedOut: false }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk rewrite exited 2' } when rewrite exits 2.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk rewrite exited 127' } when rewrite exits 127.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk rewrite timed out' } when rewrite returns { exitCode: -1, stdout: '', timedOut: true }.
createRtkInterceptor interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk rewrite failed: spawn ENOENT' } when rewrite rejects with error message 'spawn ENOENT'.
When bash: false, then interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } and rewrite is never called.
When enabled: false, then interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } and rewrite is never called.
When enabled: true, bash: true and which returns null, then interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk binary not found on PATH' } and rewrite is never called.
When enabled: true, bash: true and which throws 'boom', then interceptShell returns { kind: 'declined', reason: 'rtk probe failed: boom' }.
When createRtkInterceptor receives bash: true, then recorded InterceptorState carries bash: true.
When createRtkInterceptor is called without bash, then recorded InterceptorState carries bash: false.
When default rewrite invokes a fake PATH rtk executable that records its pid and sleeps, then it resolves with timedOut: true within RTK_REWRITE_TIMEOUT_MS plus one second.
When default rewrite times out after a fake rtk records its pid, then that pid is no longer a running process afterwards.
When default rewrite invokes a fake PATH rtk printing 'rtk bun test' and exiting 3 for rtk rewrite 'bun test', then it resolves { exitCode: 3, stdout: 'rtk bun test\n', timedOut: false }.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module configuration and provider subprocess integration with timeout and kill semantics; not itself a permission gate.

userStories.title: Run validated rtk rewrites inside native Bash
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Install the one run-scoped interceptor into Git and Bash, and execute only validated Bash rewrites after permission checks.

**Motivation** — The permission policy and the command-safety guard still judge the model's ORIGINAL command, because the rewrite happens inside the tool, after `callTool` has allowed the call.

**Approach** — `setupRun` builds ONE interceptor with `{ enabled, verbs, bash: ci.bash.enabled }` and assigns it to both `_gitToolDeps.interceptor` and `_bashToolDeps.interceptor`. `_bashToolDeps` becomes `{ runArgv, interceptor: undefined as CommandInterceptor | undefined }`. After validating `command` and before launching, `createBashTool(opts).run(input, ctx)` calls `interceptShell(command, ctx.root, _bashToolDeps.interceptor)` and launches the returned `command`; when the command was rewritten, runs `_bashToolDeps.interceptor.postProcess(stdout, { kind: "shell", command: <the model's ORIGINAL command>, cwd: ctx.root, site: "bash" })` over stdout — the same request shape `interceptShell` sent, mirroring the Git site (`git.ts:412`), which passes the original argv. `run` is already about 75 lines, so the interception, overlay and post-processing live in one helper in `src/tools/bash.ts` that `run` calls, keeping `run` within its complexity budget; `bun run check:complexity` must pass. Preserve existing framing and executed audit even on nonzero exits, and use raw stdout if postProcess throws. Document the Bash site in docs/guides/mcp-and-interception.md (Part 2: configuration row, a Scope rewrite naming both sites and why Bash is not R10's case, the validator rules, and the decline table). Restore `_bashToolDeps.interceptor` alongside `_gitToolDeps.interceptor` in setup-run tests to prevent cross-file leakage.

**Scope** — In: Bash tool interception, runtime policy ordering, run installation, post-processing and docs. Out: defining the shell validator (US-001), rtk provider/config (US-002), defining the AGENT marker rule and adding AGENT to Exec (US-004). Rewriting user-authored command strings: `quality.commands`, `acceptance.command` and every other config-supplied command stay unintercepted (R10 stands for them). Interception of `RunCommand` (Exec): it is argv-shaped and receives only the `AGENT=1` overlay in this spec. Changing the existing Git site's verbs, validation or hint stripping.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export const _bashToolDeps = { runArgv, interceptor: undefined as CommandInterceptor | undefined };
// setupRun: the same createRtkInterceptor({ enabled: ci.enabled, verbs: ci.git.verbs, bash: ci.bash.enabled }) instance is assigned to both tool deps.
```
acceptanceCriteria: When createCodingToolRuntime(...).callTool('Bash', { command: 'bun test a.test.ts' }) is granted under gated policy for bun test* and the interceptor answers 'rtk bun test a.test.ts', then _bashToolDeps.runArgv receives argv ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'rtk bun test a.test.ts'].
When that granted call is rewritten, then the interceptor's interceptShell receives the model's original command 'bun test a.test.ts'.
When callTool('Bash', { command: 'rm -rf src' }) runs under a gated policy not granting rm, then the call is denied.
When callTool('Bash', { command: 'rm -rf src' }) is denied under that gated policy, then the interceptor's interceptShell is never called.
When that granted call is rewritten, then the tool result's audit.executed equals ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'rtk bun test a.test.ts'].
When the interceptor answers invalid candidate 'rtk read src/a.ts' for 'cat src/a.ts', then runArgv receives ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'cat src/a.ts'].
When _bashToolDeps.interceptor is undefined, then runArgv receives the original command.
When _bashToolDeps.interceptor is undefined, then audit.executed equals ['/bin/sh', '-c', the original command].
When a rewritten call uses createBashTool({ launcher }), then the launcher's request carries spec: { kind: 'shell', shell: '/bin/sh', command: 'rtk bun test a.test.ts' }.
When rewritten stdout ends with '\n[full output: rtk recall 12]', then the tool result's content equals the framed output built from stdout with the hint line removed.
When a call is not rewritten and stdout ends with '\n[full output: rtk recall 12]', then that hint line remains intact in the returned output.
When a call is rewritten, then postProcess receives { kind: 'shell', command: the model's original command, cwd: ctx.root, site: 'bash' }.
When postProcess throws for a rewritten call, then the tool result's content carries raw stdout.
When a rewritten command exits 1, then the result returns isError: true with audit.exitCode === 1.
When a rewritten command exits 1, then runArgv is called exactly once (the original is never re-run).
When a real setupRun uses commandInterceptor: { enabled: true, bash: { enabled: true } }, then _bashToolDeps.interceptor is the same object as _gitToolDeps.interceptor.
When a real setupRun uses commandInterceptor: { enabled: true, bash: { enabled: true } } with a log sink, then the 'rtk interceptor state' log entry's data carries bash: true.
When a real setupRun uses default config, then _bashToolDeps.interceptor.interceptShell returns { kind: 'unchanged' } for 'bun test'.

routing.reasoning: Integrates provider-generated shell strings with a permission-gated native tool and audit ledger; execution ordering is access-control critical.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `withDepsRestore` calls (line 34) restore only `_gitToolDeps.interceptor`; once `setupRun` also assigns `_bashToolDeps.interceptor`, that module-level value leaks into later test files. US-003 adds `withDepsRestore(_bashToolDeps, ["interceptor"])` and the new `setupRun` criteria to this file. The replacing invariant: every interceptor `setupRun` installs is restored after each test.

userStories.title: Opt native Bash and Exec children into agent-friendly output
acceptanceCriteria: agentOutputOverlay([]) returns { AGENT: '1' } when _agentOutputEnvDeps.processEnv returns an environment with none of CLAUDECODE, REPL_ID, AGENT.
agentOutputOverlay([]) returns undefined when _agentOutputEnvDeps.processEnv returns an environment carrying CLAUDECODE.
agentOutputOverlay([]) returns undefined when _agentOutputEnvDeps.processEnv returns an environment carrying AGENT: '0'.
agentOutputOverlay(['AGENT']) returns undefined when no marker is inherited.
When importing withAgentOutputEnv and AGENT_OUTPUT_MARKERS from @/verification, then both are the same values as those imported from src/utils/agent-output-env.ts.
When createBashTool().run({ command: 'bun test' }, ctx) has no launcher and no inherited marker, then _bashToolDeps.runArgv receives env: { AGENT: '1' }.
When that Bash call inherits CLAUDECODE, then runArgv receives no env key.
When createBashTool({ stripEnvVars: ['AGENT'] }) runs with no inherited marker, then runArgv receives no env key.
When createBashTool({ launcher }) runs with no inherited marker, then the launcher receives env: { AGENT: '1' }.
When runExecBranch has no launcher, no Exec env and no inherited marker, then runArgv receives env: { AGENT: '1' }.
When runExecBranch has a launcher, Yarn no-scripts env and no inherited marker, then the launcher receives env: { YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS: 'false', AGENT: '1' }.
When runExecBranch inherits CLAUDECODE and has no Exec env, then its spawn receives no env key.

When an available real srt-backed createCommandLauncher runs createBashTool({ launcher }).run({ command: 'echo AGENT=$AGENT' }, ctx) with no inherited marker, then returned output carries 'AGENT=1' (skip only if probeSandbox reports srt unavailable).
When the quality runner spawns a configured command with no inherited marker, then its env carries AGENT: '1' (the moved helper keeps its behaviour).

routing.reasoning: Cross-cutting env behavior across two tools, verification compatibility and real sandbox transport; established marker rule but several integration paths.

modifiedFiles.reason: the "Yarn no-scripts env overlay survives wrapping" test (line 99) asserts the launcher's `env` equals exactly `{ YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS: "false" }`, and its result depends on whether the test process inherits `CLAUDECODE`/`AGENT`. US-004 merges the `AGENT=1` overlay into that env, so the test stubs `_agentOutputEnvDeps.processEnv` to an environment with no marker and asserts `{ YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS: "false", AGENT: "1" }`. The replacing invariant: the Yarn key survives wrapping alongside the agent-output key.

analysis: Existing TypeScript/Bun feature, not greenfield. The argv-only generic seam in src/execution/command-interceptor/index.ts:1-88 has Site='git', a CommandInterceptor with intercept/postProcess, and a fail-open interceptArgv/validateRewrite; add the shell seam in a separate type-only importing module and export it from this barrel, leaving Git's argv validation intact. src/permissions/bash-lex.ts:104-146 exposes a safe-by-refusal lexer, tokens with text/opaque, redirects, separators and segments; compare byte-exact insertions AND parsed segment tokens to avoid trusting rtk stdout as executable shell text. In particular reject both ends of a pipe, already-wrapped command words, changes to quotes/whitespace, and unlexable originals even in raw approval mode. src/execution/interceptors/rtk/index.ts:4-114 performs one synchronous PATH/version probe at construction, records state, filters Git verbs and strips only the existing RTK_HINT_LINE; add optional bash and injectable async rewrite, 2-second killable timeout, preserve existing Git callers and state logging expectations. src/config/schemas-execution.ts:221-232,320-325 uses strict zod and a default literal; src/config/schemas.ts:174-176 also derives its execution default via CommandInterceptorConfigSchema.parse({}), so extend the schema and the execution literal (not an independent hard-coded schemas.ts default); src/config/runtime-types-execution.ts:70-85 and src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:110-116 need the new field. src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:28-48,198-214 is the single rtk composition site: assign the same interceptor to Git and Bash; module-level dependency injection needs restoration between tests. src/tools/runtime.ts:310-330 checks permission before dispatch, so perform rewriting inside Bash.run, never before the gate; src/tools/bash.ts:76,238-315 has direct runArgv and launcher branches, audit.executed, framing and output cap: a helper should coordinate rewrite, AGENT overlay and post-processing before framing/truncation, retaining the actual executed command, raw output on postProcess failure, no retry after execution. src/tools/git.ts:380-435 mirrors original request in postProcess. src/tools/run-command-exec.ts:45-138 validates and normalizes argv and must receive only AGENT overlay, merged with normalized.env (not rtk). src/verification/executor.ts:40-84 has marker/withAgentOutputEnv implementation, src/quality/runner.ts:16,148 imports it through executor and must remain compatible; src/verification/index.ts:8 re-exports executor. src/sandbox/launcher.ts:103-145 already forwards env overlays on both wrapped and unwrapped paths, but its TMPDIR comment contradicts measured overlay propagation; correct it and verify against real srt, not only a stub. docs/guides/mcp-and-interception.md:156-231 currently documents Git-only scope and must explain Bash and decline rules. Existing regression tests: test/unit/execution/command-interceptor.test.ts:109 (misleading title, unchanged assertions), test/unit/execution/interceptors/rtk.test.ts (closed-world state/log checks), test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-command-interceptor.test.ts:34 (restore both injected interceptors), test/unit/tools/runtime-sandbox-audit.test.ts (policy ordering), test/unit/tools/run-command-exec-sandbox.test.ts:85-101 (Yarn exact env expectation), plus quality runner and sandbox launcher tests. Migration: no config opt-in change for existing projects, absent bash defaults false and optional provider option leaves Git behavior unchanged; AGENT overlay is intentionally unconditional for native agent-issued Bash/Exec unless inherited marker or explicit AGENT strip. Risks: execution of untrusted provider stdout, privilege bypass if rewrite runs before policy, inadvertent pipeline semantics changes, accidental rerun of a failed rewritten command, timeout child leaks, test-environment marker contamination, sandbox overlays, cross-test module dependency leakage and import cycles. Validate via isolated unit, fake-PATH integration and srt-available integration tests; existing automatic type/complexity/import-cycle gates apply.
outOfScope: Rewriting user-authored command strings: `quality.commands`, `acceptance.command` and every other config-supplied command stay unintercepted (R10 stands for them).
ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode): their own shell tools are theirs to hook; nax does not add `AGENT` to `buildAllowedEnv` and does not rewrite their commands.
A Codex-style prompt instruction telling the model to prefix `rtk` itself.

Accepting rtk rewrites that change the command word (`cat` -> `rtk read`, `npx tsc` -> `rtk tsc`), insert after a wrapper (`uv run rtk pytest`), or normalise whitespace; all are declined, and widening the validator is a separate change.
Rewriting a segment that writes into or reads from a pipe.

Adding `AGENT=1` when a marker was inherited but is removed by `quality.stripEnvVars` (e.g. `CLAUDECODE` stripped); marker presence is read from the nax process environment, the same rule `withAgentOutputEnv` applies today.
A config switch for the `AGENT=1` overlay on `Bash` and `RunCommand`; it is on for every run, like the quality and verification runners.
Stripping rtk's `[see remaining: tail ... rtk/tee/...]` hint; only the hints `RTK_HINT_LINE` already matches are stripped.
Configuring `RTK_REWRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` through `NaxConfig`; it is an exported constant.
A per-call cache of `rtk rewrite` results.
Interception of `RunCommand` (Exec): it is argv-shaped and receives only the `AGENT=1` overlay in this spec.
Changing the existing Git site's verbs, validation or hint stripping.
Verifying the env-overlay behaviour of the srt sandbox on Linux; the probe covered macOS only.
Rewriting a command the lexer refuses (command substitution, `2>&1`, subshells) under the `raw` approval mode; it runs unrewritten.
